root_cause.text: In nf_tables catchall element activation/deactivation, nft_map_catchall_activate() and nft_map_catchall_deactivate() incorrectly stopped after the first matching pending catchall entry, leaving additional live/pending catchall elements in the same map untoggled during abort/delete transactions.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `break;` from both `nft_map_catchall_deactivate()` and `nft_map_catchall_activate()`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that transaction processing can have “1 live catchall element and 1 pending element” and that when the map is removed it is necessary “to toggle all catchall elements and not just the first viable candidate,” otherwise `nft_data_release` warns during abort cleanup.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch removes the `break;` from both `nft_map_catchall_deactivate()` and `nft_map_catchall_activate()`, and the CVE/commit message explicitly states that transaction processing can have “1 live catchall element and 1 pending element” and that when the map is removed it is necessary “to toggle all catchall elements and not just the first viable candidate,” otherwise `nft_data_release` warns during abort cleanup.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix catchall deactivation to process all catchall elements instead of stopping after the first one.
intent_record.what: The diff removes a single `break;` statement from inside the loop in `nft_map_catchall_deactivate()`, so the loop no longer exits immediately after processing the first matching or iterated catchall element.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function will continue iterating through all remaining catchall entries instead of stopping after the first one, allowing every applicable element to be marked inactive and deactivated rather than only the first entry being handled.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix `nft_map_catchall_activate()` to process all catchall elements instead of stopping after the first one.
intent_record.what: The change removes the `break;` statement from inside the loop in `nft_map_catchall_activate()`, so the loop no longer exits after processing the first matching `catchall` element.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function will continue iterating through all loop entries instead of stopping after the first processed one, allowing activation and clearing logic to be applied to every relevant `catchall` element rather than only the first.

grouping_result.intent: Fix `nft_map_catchall_activate()` to process all catchall elements instead of stopping after the first one.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix nftables catchall map activation/deactivation logic so iteration processes all catchall elements instead of stopping after the first one.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly fix the stated root cause by making nft_map_catchall_activate() and nft_map_catchall_deactivate() iterate over and toggle all matching catchall elements instead of stopping after the first pending entry.

candidates.rationale: This premature loop termination in catchall deactivation causes only the first matching pending catchall element to be toggled, leaving additional live/pending catchall elements unchanged.

This premature loop termination in catchall activation causes iteration to stop after the first matching catchall element, so remaining catchall elements in the same map are not activated during transaction handling.

vuln_statements.explanation: This premature loop termination caused nft_map_catchall_activate() and nft_map_catchall_deactivate() to stop after the first matching pending catchall entry, leaving additional live/pending catchall elements in the same map untoggled during abort/delete transaction handling.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it includes both relevant functions, `nft_map_catchall_deactivate()` and `nft_map_catchall_activate()`, showing their full loop logic over `set->catchall_list`. Both functions iterate with `list_for_each_entry(catchall, &set->catchall_list, list)`, test `if (!nft_set_elem_active(ext, genmask)) continue;`, perform the activate/deactivate operation on the matching element, and then immediately `break;`. Specifically, in `nft_map_catchall_deactivate()` after `nft_setelem_data_deactivate(ctx->net, set, &elem);` there is a `break;`, and in `nft_map_catchall_activate()` after `nft_setelem_data_activate(ctx->net, set, &elem);` there is also a `break;`. The root cause says these functions should not stop after the first matching pending catchall entry because that leaves additional live/pending catchall elements untoggled. This exact vulnerable construct is present here. Therefore `has_bug=true`. Since the code still contains the premature `break;` instead of processing all matching catchall entries, the fix is not present, so `is_fixed=false`.
